body:
Thanks for your report @mzh3511 
When running in Visual Studio using the test adapter, I can confirm I can see this behaviour on net472 which your repro targets. I can't reproduce this on .NET8, indicating it could be an issue specific to when it runs on .NET Framework.

@nunit/framework-team 
It can be reproduced by any test which causes the comparer chain to _try_ the `StreamsComparer`, regardless of if it's needed or not. For example, since we test numerics _after_ streams in the [NUnitEqualityComparer](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/c9fe0e704ce67ad70bf72ccdeae05d4105a2428c/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Constraints/NUnitEqualityComparer.cs), the following will _also_ cause this to fail:

```csharp
        [Test]
        public void Test1()
        {
            Assert.That(1, Is.EqualTo(1));
        }
```

Trying to apply this binding redirect:
```xml
<dependentAssembly>
	<assemblyIdentity name="System.Buffers"
	  publicKeyToken="cc7b13ffcd2ddd51"
	  culture="neutral" />
	<bindingRedirect oldVersion="0.0.0.0-4.6.0.0" newVersion="4.6.0.0" />
	<publisherPolicy apply="no" />
</dependentAssembly>
```

will produce the following build warning:
> Found conflicts between different versions of "System.Buffers" that could not be resolved.
There was a conflict between "System.Buffers, Version=4.0.4.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51" and "System.Buffers, Version=4.6.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51".
    "System.Buffers, Version=4.0.4.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51" was chosen because it was primary and "System.Buffers, Version=4.6.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51" was not.

@nunit/framework-team Assuming that binding is correct then the "chosen because it was primary" warning is curious. We don't explicitly define `System.Buffers` as a dependency but we do pull it in transitively via `System.Memory`. Should we define it?
I've pushed my testing here: https://github.com/nunit/nunit.issues/tree/main/Issue4887

Hello @stevenaw,
the binding redirect is working for the execution with Visual Studio but not when i execute the tests with the nunit-console.

Can we update System.Buffers or System.Memory to the new version in the nunit project? 
Than everything should function again.

@sba-schleupen We're looking into it :)

@mzh3511 Does it work for you as a workaround for now to explicitly target version 4.5.5 of `System.Memory`  instead  version 4.6.0 of `System.Buffers`? That should at least pull in the `System.Buffers` reference you need in a way that at least seemed to work for me in the repro project.

For example:

```diff
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="JetBrains.dotMemoryUnit" Version="3.2.20220510" />
    <PackageReference Include="MathNet.Spatial" Version="0.6.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.3.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="NUnit" Version="4.2.2" />
    <PackageReference Include="NUnit3TestAdapter" Version="4.6.0" />
-   <PackageReference Include="System.Buffers" Version="4.6.0" />
+   <PackageReference Include="System.Memory" Version="4.5.5" />
  </ItemGroup>
```

@stevenaw It is the package System.Memory including System.Buffers as a dependency, which was included March 20th in PR #4668 meant to improve performance of the StreamsComparer.   Version 4.1. was in February, so this was introduced in version 4.2.   The version of System.Memory now is 4.5.5, and it references System.Buffers 4.5.1.   But for framework .net 6, we see version 6.0.0 of the System.Buffers.  So the package we refer to seems to be needed only for .net framework.  

In the nuspec file we conditionally include System.Memory only for .net framework.

I can't see any good reason not to upgrade System.Memory to 4.6.0, which will also upgrade System.Buffers to the same version. 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cef8616-3a66-4b6c-99cb-9472a169a568)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c9c4df0-55dc-42c4-9168-d17313db044f)

Btw:  We might have a risk with System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions too, we include version 4.5.4, but the latest release is 4.6.0.  Again, only .net framework.

body:
Unfortunately in the System.Memory files MS has done something weird with the versioning. The NuGet version and the AssemblyVersion are out of sync. 
* System.Memory
  * NuGet 4.6.0 => AssemblyVersion is 4.0.2.0
  * NuGet 4.5.5 => AssemblyVersion is 4.0.1.2

* System.Buffer
  * NuGet 4.6.0 => AssemblyVersion 4.0.4.0
  * NuGet 4.5.1 => AssemblyVersion 4.0.3.0

@SFrank1966 Does you project indirectly reference a different version of System.Buffers? I see 4.6.1 is out.

With .NET (Framework) if any referenced project uses a different version you need to explicitly redirect that one to yours.
.NET doesn't load another version of signed assemblies as it might break things.

Note that the redirect reference the AssemblyVersion, not the NuGet version!

```xml
<dependentAssembly>
	<assemblyIdentity name="System.Buffers"
	  publicKeyToken="cc7b13ffcd2ddd51"
	  culture="neutral" />
	<bindingRedirect oldVersion="0.0.0.0-4.0.5.0" newVersion="4.0.5.0" />
	<publisherPolicy apply="no" />
</dependentAssembly>
```

At my work we have a whole file of redirects to maintain for all shared project we use (most of them our own) as libraries update at different times. As long as we don't have major version changes with breaking changes even though annoying, it works.

@nunit/core-team We might want to reconsider removing this dependency as there will be both users that use earlier and later versions of System.Memory/System.Buffers.
